answer: During a 3 hour outage last quarter every queued grade went to whichever panel happened to be online, and 12 of 60 verdicts came back wrong. The fix splits each grade across independent auditors, so no single pool sees a whole verdict, and a random spot check re-grades one in twenty. A reviewer who misses a spot check loses stake. Trust sits on a finished task, not on the age of an address, and the trellis holding it up is the auditor split between the grove of verified work and the ocean of claims.
